title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing, fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Ravi Sundaram
description: Motivation: The continuous-batcher scheduler has shown uneven request latencies under mixed workloads. Small, latency-sensitive requests were being starved by larger batched streams and long-waiting queues. This PR tunes queueing, fairness, and timeout behavior to reduce tail latency and avoid starvation while preserving batching efficiency. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce a multi-queue scheduler with priority lanes: latency-sensitive (low token count / interactive) and throughput lanes (large seqs). 2) Add dynamic aging to avoid starvation: requests increment priority based on wait time with configurable decay/thresholds. 3) Implement per-request soft and hard timeouts: soft timeout triggers auto-flush for small queues, hard timeout forces a fallback to single-request execution when necessary. 4) Adaptive batch sizing changes: reduce batch size growth heuristics for mixed traffic to favor faster dispatch of small requests. 5) Observability hooks: new metrics for per-lane queue length, age percentiles, and timeout/ejection counts; traces include lane and aging decisions. 6) Config surface: new scheduler config struct and defaults; kept backward compatible and gated behind a feature flag in runtime config. Performance results: In a 48-hour mixed workload replay (30% small interactive requests, 70% long seq bulk requests) on a 4xA100 Dedicated pool we observed: - 95th percentile latency for small requests reduced from 210ms -> 95ms (-55%) - 99th percentile latency reduced from 540ms -> 170ms (-68%) - End-to-end token throughput impact: ~2% reduction at peak, but 20% fewer SLA violations for latency-sensitive routes. Testing and validation: unit tests for scheduling logic and deterministic aging, integration tests with batcher simulator, end-to-end canary on perf-canary infra for two days, and additional load tests against continuous-batcher in redwood/perf-canary. Rollout plan: behind feature flag by default disabled; enable for a small percentage of hosts (canary) then ramp to 25% over 48h, monitor new metrics and rollback on elevated ejection/timeouts. Related: closes ENG-2345 and references previous PRs on continuous-batcher fairness (see pr-61422, pr-31024). Backwards compatibility: runtime API unchanged; config additions are optional. Risk: aggressive aging could reduce batching efficiency on pure-throughput workloads - mitigated by config knobs and canary rollout. Documentation: scheduler behaviour and new config documented in docs/schedulers/continuous-batcher.md (included).
